svg.title: The machine: wiring
svg.text: 2 x PZ7020 FPGA + Teensy 4.1 with 8 PSRAM + 2 x STM32H743 + ESP32-P4
Cables and cards. The only wire is the speaker lead on the ESP32-P4.
The PC's Ethernet stays on the internet: the PC connects to the machine by USB consoles only.
1. Do it in this order (bench day)
Card #1 (32 GB) in FPGA #1's underside slot, card #2 (32 GB) in FPGA #2 -- both written by me with the machine image
beforehand. Boot jumper cap on SD on both (right-hand pair, beside the USB-A port).
Ethernet, FPGA #1 UPPER jack <-> FPGA #2 UPPER jack. A normal cable; no switch.
FPGA #1 LOWER USB-C (J2) -> PC USB. FPGA #2 LOWER USB-C (J2) -> PC USB. These are consoles; they do NOT power the
Teensy micro-USB -> PC USB. It boots, proves its PSRAM and waits. Leave it.
I arm the watcher on both consoles and the Teensy.
5 V (USB-A -> USB-C cable) -> FPGA #1 UPPER USB-C (J8). FPGA #1 boots: the first Linux boot this board has ever done.
I read its report (about a minute).
5 V -> FPGA #2 UPPER USB-C (J8). I check the link between the two over cable 1.
from FPGA #1's console: engine, link, model, Teensy. You do nothing.
Phase 2, one board at a time, when I ask:
STM32 #1, STM32 #2, ESP32-P4 -- pages 6 to 8. Never before.
unplug the 5 V from J8 first, then the consoles. Never unplug the Teensy while it is reading its card.
phase 2: a USB hub for the
top view · card #1 underneath · jumper on SD
top view · card #2 underneath · jumper on SD
Teensy -> PC: a data cable, it powers the Teensy
12 HDMI from FPGA #1 to any monitor: optional (the GPU's screen).
solid = today. dashed orange = phase 2, only when I ask. Cards: #1 and #2 are 32 GB; the Teensy keeps its own.
FPGA #1 UPPER Ethernet jack <-> FPGA #2 UPPER Ethernet jack.
Normal Ethernet cable, direct, no switch. #1 = 10.20.0.2, #2 = 10.20.0.3. The engines' link.
Console only (CH340). It does not power the board. The watcher records the boot.
A DATA cable, not charge-only. Powers the Teensy and its PSRAM. Only flash it with the PC idle.
5 V supply A -> FPGA #1 UPPER USB-C (J8).
USB-A -> USB-C cable. A C-to-C cable gives this board NO power. Plug this LAST, when I say.
5 V supply B -> FPGA #2 UPPER USB-C (J8).
Nothing else today. No jumper wires. Not the JM1/JM2 headers. Not the lower Ethernet jacks. Not the USB-A ports.
4. Cable by cable: phase 2 (only when I ask, one board at a time)
STM32 #1 console USB-C (the one by the CH340 chip) -> PC USB hub.
Flashing and console. Powers the board.
STM32 #1 other USB-C (OTG) -> FPGA #1 USB-A host port.
Its data link into the machine (USB serial). Plug after the console.
STM32 #2 console USB-C -> PC USB hub.
STM32 #2 other USB-C (OTG) -> FPGA #2 USB-A host port.
ESP32-P4 RJ45 -> FPGA #2 LOWER Ethernet jack (ETH-PL).
Only after I have switched eth1 on (a boot-file change, tested on FPGA #1 first).
8 ohm speaker -> ESP32-P4 speaker header (MX1.25, 2 pins).
The one wire on this machine. Polarity does not matter for a lone speaker.
The GPU's screen: colour bars, then dark blue.
5. The FPGA board: which port is which (both boards are identical)
JM1 40-pin header (top edge) - nothing on it
JM2 40-pin header (bottom edge) - nothing on it
top view, as it sits on the bench
the SD card slot is UNDERNEATH
5 V IN (also JTAG). USB-A -> C cable only.
console (CH340), to the PC. No power.
boot jumper: cap on the RIGHT pair = SD
LEDs: PWR on with 5 V. DONE lights when the PL bitstream loads (about 5 s after power).
If DONE never lights: the card or the jumper. Tell me; do not press anything.
6. Teensy 4.1 with the eight PSRAM: nothing new to wire
Teensy 4.1 + 8 x ESP-PSRAM64H on the perfboard (docs/47)
microSD in the Teensy's own slot: the 3B model (qwen3b.gguf) as today
micro-USB -> PC: data cable. That is all.
It runs psram_llm v9g: at power-up it proves every chip and waits for a prompt.
Later: the machine's small model added to its card, so it checks the engines' answers exactly.
Rules that stand: flash only with the PC idle; never unplug it while it is reading the card (the card hangs until a USB power-cycle).
two USB-C on the short edge · two LCD ribbon sockets (not used) · TF slot on the back
TF card (back): 4 GB, the small model file on it (I prepare the card).
SWD 4-pin, LCD sockets, pin headers: nothing.
Which USB-C is which: the one next to the small 16-pin CH340 chip is the console.
Send a photo of both sides' silkscreen before phase 2: I need the vendor pins.
100 Mbit RJ45, USB-A (host/device), USB-C console, audio amp + speaker header, TF slot, 40-pin header
after eth1 is on; 100 Mbit is plenty for text
No screen is owned, so it is a panel by web page and sound, not a display.
9. What you should see, and what to do about it
its LED blinks while it proves the PSRAM (about 30 s), then the console shows 'I bench-one psram_llm v9 banks N'.
Nothing to do. If banks < 6 I decide.
PWR LED on; DONE LED on within ~5 s; console: SPL banner, U-Boot, kernel, then 'ZYNQ-REPORT' after ~60 s.
Wait for me. This is the board's first Linux boot.
no console text within 20 s of 5 V.
Unplug the 5 V. Check the card is seated and the jumper is on the right pair. Tell me; I do not guess at it.
PWR on, console alive, but DONE dark.
Tell me. pl.bit did not load; the engine will report 'cpu' instead of 'pl' and I will know.
both jacks' link LEDs on once both boards are up.
If not: reseat the cable. Any straight or crossover cable works (auto-MDIX).
runs from FPGA #1's console; takes 5 to 30 minutes depending on what the cards hold.
Do nothing. I report once at the end, with the log archived.
